//: Airlyhub Realtime Database security rules.
Deploy:  firebase deploy --only database
RTDB holds user avatars and support-chat attachments, because the free plan
provisions no Cloud Storage bucket. Each node is one base64 image; the owning
record lives in Firestore and carries just the path.
Design notes:
- Denied at the root, granted one path at a time, mirroring firestore.rules.
- Grants sit on the leaf, never on `$uid`. RTDB rules cascade downward — a `.read`
one level up would let a client pull every attachment the user ever sent in a
single request, which on a metered free plan is the whole egress budget.
- `!data.exists()` makes a node write-once: no overwrite, and no delete either,
since a delete is a write of null over existing data. That matches the messages
rule in Firestore, where a sent message is a record neither side can revise.
Avatars are the deliberate exception — see below.
- The length cap is base64 of the client's 512 KB limit (512 * 1024 * 4/3, rounded
up for padding). Enforced here too, because a client-side cap protects nobody.
Readable by any signed-in user: an avatar is shown next to its owner, so
restricting it to the owner would leave every other view with a placeholder.
Unlike chatAttachments this is neither write-once nor append-only. A profile
photo is current state rather than a record, so the owner may overwrite it,
and `!newData.exists()` admits the delete that removing an avatar performs.
